newsitem.title: UK: Russia Eurobond to be 10-yr for at least $1.0 bln.
newsitem.headline: Russia Eurobond to be 10-yr for at least $1.0 bln.

text.p: Russia's next Eurobond is likely to have a 10-year maturity and be for at least $1.0 billion, deputy minister of finance Mikhail Kasyanov said on Friday.
"On the basis of our analysis of market reception we are looking for a 10-year term and a size of not less than $1.0 billion," he said at a press conference.
Russian officials were in London to meet investors ahead of their forthcoming Eurobond. Roadshows for the deal end on June 18, and launch is expected soon after.
J.P. Morgan and SBC Warburg are joint lead managers for the transaction.
London-based bankers said on Thursday a 10-year Russian Eurobond could be priced to yield around 375 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes.

Russia first tapped the international capital markets in November 1996, when it launched a $1.0 billion five-year bond at 345 b.p. over Treasuries. The bond was recently trading at around 275 b.p. over.
In March, it raised 2.0 billion marks via a seven-year bond.
Russia is expected to launch a global dollar bond in the autumn. Russia's 1998 budget plans foresee $3.0 billion in Eurobond issues next year.
